intro: Job asks one of life's hardest questions: why do good people suffer?
Chapters one and two: Job loses everything, though he has done nothing wrong. Chapters three to thirty-seven: a long, poetic debate, as Job and his friends argue about why.
Chapters thirty-eight to forty-two: God himself answers, out of a whirlwind.
Its author and date aren't known. It's one of the oldest stories in the Bible.
Most of it is poetry, so let the words wash over you. Listen for Job's honesty with God, and his hope: I know that my redeemer liveth.
